docs.title: move_joints
docs.text:
Queued EXEC mode Enabled Homed Takes control

Move every joint to a target angle, in joint space. All joints start and arrive together, so the tool's path is not a straight line. Use move_linear() for a straight line.

The robot needs no inverse kinematics along the way, so a joint move also passes through singular poses, where a straight-line move can fail.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: robot.move_joints(*angles_deg, timeout=120.0, **options)

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Name Type Default Description *angles_deg float required The target angle of each joint, J1 first, in degrees. Each must lie within its joint's limits, or the move is refused before anything moves. A single list or tuple of the angles works too. timeout float 120.0 Seconds to wait for the move to finish, in sync mode only. **options Any each setting's own Settings for this move only. Each one you leave out takes its default: speed = 100 % accel = 100 % duration = none (the speed decides) profile = "ruckig" jerk = 100 % ramp_fraction = 0.25 blend = 0 blend_mode = "exact_velocity" blend_continuity = "c1" ik_solver = "pinocchio" singularity_strategy = "stop" samples = automatic dry_run = False ik_solver, singularity_strategy and samples have no effect on a joint move. (a) move_joints (b) move_linear Figure 1 The same start and end poses. A joint move's tool path curves; a straight-line move's path does not.

docs.title: Returns
docs.text:
str

The command id. The call returns once the robot has accepted the move; call wait_idle() to wait until it has finished. In sync mode the call returns when the move has finished.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
robot.move_joints(90, -105, 165, 0, -30, 180)
robot.move_joints([90, -105, 165, 0, -30, 180], speed=0.2)
robot.wait_idle()
Usage restrictions 19 codes

This command is added to the robot's motion queue. The robot accepts it only when it is ready for motion (EXEC mode, enabled and homed), from the client that holds control or when no client does. Otherwise, the robot refuses it with one of:

  • [6010] Command not allowed now — the message names the mode or state it needs
  • [6101] Control held by another client
  • [5002] Program aborted — an earlier move failed; clear errors first
  • [6004] Invalid motion options — a setting is unknown, out of range, or refused for a single move
  • [6011] Motion queue full

Once accepted, the move can still fail before it starts:

  • [5006] Move outside the joint limits — a target angle is outside its joint's limits
  • [5007] Move into a safety zone — the path would enter a safety zone
  • [5008] Zone check unavailable — safety zones are active, but the robot model to check them is missing
  • [1401] Self-collision — the path would bring two parts of the arm too close
  • [5010] Requested duration too short — duration is shorter than the limits allow
  • [5011] Invalid duration — duration is not more than 0 seconds
  • [5201] TOPPRA profile unavailable — profile="toppra", but that planner is missing
  • [5202] TOPPRA found no solution — profile="toppra" found no timing within the limits
  • [5009] Planned acceleration over its limit — the planned motion would exceed an acceleration limit
  • [5001] Trajectory planning failed
  • [3201] Trajectory not taken by RTI

A move that has started can end early with:

  • [5003] Command cancelled — an earlier move failed, or the robot left EXEC mode
  • [5004] Command stopped — stop() was called
  • [5005] Move did not settle — only with set_completion_policy("strict")

In Python, a refusal raises CommandRejected; its number is the code above. A failure after the robot accepted the move is raised by wait_idle() as MotionFailed, or by this call itself in sync mode as CommandRejected. No answer raises RobotTimeout; no connection, RobotConnectionError.

docs.title: Protocol
docs.text:
A client that does not use robotclient sends this over the TCP command protocol (port 29000) for the example above:

{"id": "c1", "cmd": "move_joints", "args": [90.0, -105.0, 165.0, 0.0, -30.0, 180.0]}

docs.text: move_linear wait_idle move_pose set_joint_speed Per-move settings

docs.title: move_pose
docs.text:
Queued EXEC mode Enabled Homed Takes control

Move the tool to a pose, with the joints moving in joint space. The robot works out the joint angles for the pose, starting from where the arm is, then moves there like move_joints(): the tool's path is not a straight line. Use move_linear() for a straight line, and is_reachable() to check a pose first.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: robot.move_pose(x, y, z, rx, ry, rz, timeout=120.0, *, angle_unit='rad', **options)

docs.title: move_spline_rel_world
docs.text:
Queued EXEC mode Enabled Homed Takes control

Move the tool along a smooth curve through offsets along the base axes. Like move_spline(), with each waypoint given as an offset from where the tool is when the move starts, along axes parallel to the base frame. Each offset is from that start point, not from the previous waypoint.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: robot.move_spline_rel_world(waypoints, timeout=120.0, *, angle_unit='rad', **options)

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Name Type Default Description waypoints Sequence[Sequence[float]] required Two or more offsets [dx, dy, dz, drx, dry, drz]: metres, and radians or degrees as angle_unit says. timeout float 120.0 Seconds to wait for the move to finish, in sync mode only. angle_unit str 'rad' "rad" or "deg": the unit of every angle in this call. **options Any each setting's own Settings for this move only. Each one you leave out takes its default: speed = 100 % accel = 100 % duration = none (the speed decides) profile = "ruckig" jerk = 100 % ramp_fraction = 0.25 blend = 0 blend_mode = "exact_velocity" blend_continuity = "c1" ik_solver = "pinocchio" singularity_strategy = "stop" samples = automatic dry_run = False

docs.title: Returns
docs.text:
str

The command id. The call returns once the robot has accepted the move; call wait_idle() to wait until it has finished. In sync mode the call returns when the move has finished.

docs.title: Further details
docs.text:
Note

Blending does not apply: blend must be 0, and the move starts and ends at rest. A curve that would exceed an acceleration limit is slowed down, to 25 % of speed at most, before it fails; with duration set it is not slowed.

Usage restrictions 29 codes

This command is added to the robot's motion queue. The robot accepts it only when it is ready for motion (EXEC mode, enabled and homed), from the client that holds control or when no client does. Otherwise, the robot refuses it with one of:

  • [6022] Client too old for pose commands — only a raw client that sends no "protocol": 1
  • [6010] Command not allowed now — the message names the mode or state it needs
  • [6101] Control held by another client
  • [5002] Program aborted — an earlier move failed; clear errors first
  • [6004] Invalid motion options — a setting is unknown, out of range, or refused for a single move
  • [6011] Motion queue full

Once accepted, the move can still fail before it starts:

  • [5108] Blending not supported on curves — blend is above 0; curves do not blend yet
  • [5110] Invalid curve arguments — a raw client sent the wrong number of values
  • [5109] Invalid curve — fewer than two waypoints differ from each other and from the start
  • [5101] Target out of reach — the arm cannot reach the target pose
  • [5102] Path only partly reachable — the arm cannot reach a pose on the way to the target
  • [5103] Path too close to a limit — a pose on the path needs a joint outside its limits
  • [5105] Configuration flip on the path — the arm would have to change its configuration on the way, for example flip its wrist
  • [5104] Solution misses the pose — the joint solution misses a pose on the path
  • [5107] Tool strays from the path — the tool would stray from the curve, usually near a singularity
  • [5010] Requested duration too short — duration is shorter than the limits allow
  • [5011] Invalid duration — duration is not more than 0 seconds
  • [5201] TOPPRA profile unavailable — profile="toppra", but that planner is missing
  • [5202] TOPPRA found no solution — profile="toppra" found no timing within the limits
  • [5009] Planned acceleration over its limit — the planned motion would exceed an acceleration limit
  • [5006] Move outside the joint limits — the path would take a joint outside its limits
  • [5007] Move into a safety zone — the path would enter a safety zone
  • [5008] Zone check unavailable — safety zones are active, but the robot model to check them is missing
  • [1401] Self-collision — the path would bring two parts of the arm too close
  • [5001] Trajectory planning failed
  • [3201] Trajectory not taken by RTI

A move that has started can end early with:

  • [5003] Command cancelled — an earlier move failed, or the robot left EXEC mode
  • [5004] Command stopped — stop() was called
  • [5005] Move did not settle — only with set_completion_policy("strict")

In Python, a refusal raises CommandRejected; its number is the code above. A failure after the robot accepted the move is raised by wait_idle() as MotionFailed, or by this call itself in sync mode as CommandRejected. No answer raises RobotTimeout; no connection, RobotConnectionError. ValueError: Fewer than two waypoints, a waypoint without 6 values, or an angle_unit other than "rad" or "deg".

docs.text:
A client that does not use robotclient sends this over the TCP command protocol (port 29000) for the example above:

docs.title: delay
docs.text:
Queued EXEC mode Takes control

Wait a given time between two queued moves. The pause is queued like a move: the arm stops and holds still for seconds after the moves queued before it, then the next move starts.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: robot.delay(seconds, timeout=120.0, **options)

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Name Type Default Description seconds float required How long to wait, in seconds; more than 0. timeout float 120.0 Seconds to wait for the move to finish, in sync mode only. **options Any each setting's own Settings for this move only. Each one you leave out takes its default: speed = 100 % accel = 100 % duration = none (the speed decides) profile = "ruckig" jerk = 100 % ramp_fraction = 0.25 blend = 0 blend_mode = "exact_velocity" blend_continuity = "c1" ik_solver = "pinocchio" singularity_strategy = "stop" samples = automatic dry_run = False

docs.text:
str

The command id. The call returns once the robot has accepted the pause; call wait_idle() to wait until it has finished. In sync mode the call returns when the pause has finished.

robot.delay(0.5)
